title: Bucky's Blokes
subtitle: The 19-point market checklist, rebuilt from FRED data
as_of_note: Statuses and reads written Oct 20 2026. Numbers in braces refresh on every build.

items.heading: Interest Rates
items.subtitle: Percent, monthly
items.status: The 10-year yields {last}% and the 30-year mortgage {last2}%. The 2011 worry was a 4% yield. 2026 is past 5%.
items.question: At 5%, are bonds now competing with stocks for the same dollar?

items.heading: Jobs / Economy
items.subtitle: Percent of labor force, monthly
items.status: Unemployment is {last}%, against {yago}% a year ago. Industrial production rose 0.7% in September, its best month since April.
items.question: Is the job market cooling, or just catching its breath?

items.heading: Retail
items.subtitle: Year-over-year percent change, monthly
items.status: Retail sales are up {last}% from a year ago, against {yago}% the year before.
items.question: Is the shopper spending a raise, or savings?

items.heading: Europe
items.subtitle: Year-over-year percent change, quarterly
items.status: Euro area real GDP grew {last}% over the past year. The IMF sees 1.1% for 2026. France's public debt runs 119% of GDP.
items.question: Can Europe grow while its biggest borrowers fight their bond markets?

items.heading: Credit (Sovereign)
items.subtitle: 10-year government bond yield spreads over Germany, percentage points, monthly
items.status: France pays {last} points more than Germany to borrow for 10 years. Italy pays {last2}. Paris now looks more like Rome.
items.question: When France borrows like Italy, who is the core of Europe?

items.heading: Credit (Part Deux, Corporate)
items.subtitle: Percentage points, monthly
items.status: Baa corporate bonds pay {last} points over Treasuries, near the tight end of two decades. Yet CoreWeave's bonds yield above 15%.
items.question: Tight spreads on average, 15% on the AI borrowers. Which one is the canary?

items.heading: Geopolitical
items.subtitle: Dollars per barrel, monthly
items.status: WTI crude is ${last} a barrel, against ${yago} a year ago. The Iran war began in February. The IMF's downside case is $130.
items.question: How much of the war premium is still in the barrel?

items.heading: Monetary Policy
items.subtitle: Percent, monthly
items.status: Fed funds run {last}%, inside a 3.75% to 4.00% target. Yardeni argues the neutral rate has risen.
items.question: If neutral moved up, is today's Fed tight at all?

items.heading: Tightening Abroad
items.subtitle: Government bond yields, percent, monthly
items.status: Japan's 10-year yields {last}%, the UK's {last2}%. Japan holds $1.1 trillion of Treasuries.
items.question: When Japan pays 3% at home, does its money stay in America?

items.heading: Protectionism, Trade and Currency Wars
items.subtitle: Billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted annual rate, quarterly
items.status: Tariffs now bring in ${last} billion a year, against ${yago} billion a year earlier.
items.question: Who really pays the tariff: the exporter, the importer, or the shopper?

items.heading: Housing
items.subtitle: Year-over-year percent change, monthly
items.status: Home prices are {last}% higher than a year ago, with mortgage rates near 7.4%.
items.question: With mortgages near 7.4%, who is buying the house?

items.heading: Sentiment
items.subtitle: Index, 1966 Q1 = 100, monthly
items.status: Consumer sentiment reads {last}, near record lows, while stocks sit near highs.
items.question: When the mood is this sour, who is left to sell?

items.heading: Technical
items.subtitle: Index, weekly, with 40-week (about 200-day) average, ratio scale
items.status: The S&P 500 stands at {last}. Semiconductors fell 15.7% over eight sessions this month before bouncing.
items.question: Earnings at records, multiples shrinking. Which force wins the next leg?

items.heading: Deflation
items.subtitle: Dollars per metric ton, monthly
items.status: Copper sells for ${last} a ton, against ${yago} a year ago. Deflation is not 2026's worry.
items.question: Data centers eat copper. Is this a cycle or a new floor?

items.heading: Speculation
items.subtitle: Dollars, weekly, ratio scale
items.status: Bitcoin trades at ${last}, against ${yago} a year ago.
items.question: Is Boss Hog still binging, or finally paying back the loan?

items.heading: Underwritings
items.subtitle: Trillions of dollars, quarterly, ratio scale
items.status: Federal debt totals ${last} trillion. Net interest of $1.05 trillion now tops defense spending.
items.question: The biggest underwriting on Earth is Washington's. Who buys the next trillion?

items.heading: Wall Street
items.subtitle: Thousands of jobs, monthly
items.status: Securities and investment firms employ {last} thousand people, against {yago} thousand a year ago.
items.question: Is Wall Street hiring for the boom, or for the cleanup?

items.heading: Dr. Doom vs. the Sunshine Boys
items.subtitle: Percent, Chauvet-Piger model, monthly
items.status: The Chauvet-Piger model puts recession odds at {last}%. The Sunshine Boys have the data, for now.
items.question: When the doom model reads near zero, is that the moment to worry?

items.heading: The Media
items.subtitle: Index, weekly
items.status: The VIX reads {last}, against {yago} a year ago. Calm enough for the TV to stay cheerful.
items.question: If fear is this cheap, who is selling the insurance?
